segments.text: Retro. Not the release retro, we haven't shipped. The three-week retro, because a lot happened. Format: where we are, what went well, what didn't, lessons. Then November, briefly.
Where we are. Priya.
The UPI flow is done. Delivered Monday the 28th, one-time and mandates, tested against the Razorpay sandbox. The PayU swap is in progress, on track for tomorrow.
Rahul.
Drawer merged on the 23rd. Offline mode demoed end to end on Monday the 28th, on the Meridian devices, sync and conflicts, it held up. The Razorpay SDK is gone.
Sana.
Onboarding is built, Rahul finished it Friday. The consent screen was delivered Monday the 28th. Everything has been through the checklist.
And I did the Kestrel call this morning with Sana. More on that later. So. What went well.
Offline mode, honestly. The spike paid for itself. Deciding local-first on day one meant I never had to rethink it.
The checklist as a baseline. Once we said Meridian's checklist is the bar, every review got shorter. Nobody argued about button sizes again.
Putting the payment provider behind an interface. If I hadn't, the PayU switch would have been three weeks, not one.
Agreed on all three. What didn't go well. I'll start: the Razorpay decision.
Yeah. Can we talk about that properly? And actually, before that, I want to make sure I understand the drawer thing. Why did we choose the side drawer again?
Because the tab bar couldn't fit five sections, right? You wanted room for the Kestrel screens later.
No, that's not it. Kestrel didn't exist when we decided the drawer. It was Meridian's accessibility checklist.
Fifty-six dp minimum touch targets on their five inch devices. The tab bar came out at forty-eight.
We reversed the kickoff decision at the design review on the 16th, because of Meridian's accessibility checklist. Discoverability lost to the contract.
Oh. Yes. Sorry, I was conflating it with the Kestrel conversation. You're right, it was the fifty-six dp rule.
See, this is exactly my point. Two weeks, and we already have two different stories for one decision. Imagine in six months.
Which is a lesson. Hold that thought. Razorpay first.
We chose Razorpay at kickoff because it was the fastest UPI integration and we'd used it before. We never asked Meridian's compliance team.
Business said no preference, and we took that as the answer.
And I want to be fair to past us. No preference sounded like an answer.
It did. It wasn't. So, lesson one: confirm vendor constraints with the customer's compliance team before choosing a vendor. Not the business side. Compliance.
Agreed.
What else didn't go well. Priya, the UPI flow slips. Not blaming. Just, what do we learn?
Two slips. The 24th to the 25th was Razorpay's sandbox callbacks. The 25th to the 28th was their KYC for mandates.
Neither was code. Both were vendor lead times I didn't know about.
What I'd do differently: the second time it slipped, we should have cut mandates from the release right then, instead of giving it a new date.
We got lucky the KYC came through.
I said that in the email and then didn't do it. So, lesson two: a commitment that slips twice gets a scope cut, not a third date.
That's going to hurt someday.
That's the point.
Can I add one? The drawer confusion just now. We make decisions in meetings and the rationale lives in someone's head.
Yes. Lesson three: record the rationale with every decision, in the meeting, in the notes. Not the decision alone. The why.
And who said it.
And who said it. Rahul, that's what the decision log is for, issue forty-two. The three lessons go in there too.
On it. Friday, like I said in the email.
Those are the three. Vendor constraints from compliance. Two slips means a cut. Rationale with every decision.
Is don't trust a sandbox a lesson or just a scar?
A scar. Okay. November, briefly.
Kestrel call this morning. A hundred and twenty drivers, iOS, pilot starts November 16th. And I asked about compliance first. They have no vendor mandate, PayU is fine with them.
Decision: the Kestrel pilot uses PayU too. One provider, one integration.
Their onboarding is different, though. Drivers get a vehicle check screen, not PIN setup. I'll explore a Kestrel onboarding variant by Wednesday, October 7th.
Good. Decision: the November release scope is iOS and the Kestrel pilot. Nothing else until October ships.
iOS means I need a Mac that isn't from 2019.
Put it in the budget request. Code freeze stays October 9th, release stays the 16th. No changes there.
PayU integration tomorrow, October 1st. Still on.
Good. I'll write up the retro notes with all three lessons and the rationale, and send them tonight, so by October 1st.
With the rationale.
With the rationale. Thanks, everyone. A good three weeks, mostly.
Mostly.
